newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt lower as "rate fantasy" evaporates.
newsitem.headline: German debt lower as "rate fantasy" evaporates.

text.p: German Bund futures were convincingly lower in late trade in line with weaker U.S. Treasury prices and the growing belief that the Bundesbank is unlikely to cut interest rates any time soon.
The DTB Bund future was down 13 basis points in late trade at 99.34, but well off a low of the day of 99.26.
Bunds were pushed lower in late trade as Treausries tested sesssion lows after a drop in jobless claims.
But traders said the real drag on the market is the perception that official interest rates are indeed on hold.
The Bundesbank had been trying to keep hopes of lower rates alive, but chief economist Otmar Issing on Wednesday dashed those hopes saying rates are fine the way they are.

His comments were backed up by the central bank's decision to keep rates on hold at its regular council meeting today and the preliminary west German consumer consumer price report which showed no change from the month before.

"For the remainder of this year, inflation should oscillate around 1.5 percent, preventing a further decline in official rates, at the same time not putting the Bundesbank under pressure to raise rates," UBS said in a commentary.
Today's decline reflected a shift in market sentiment with a growing number of traders seeing downside risk to Bund prices only days after the outlook had been markedly upbeat.
Some see a risk the contract could retreat back to 99.10 and others do not even rule out a decline all the way back to 99.00 by early next week.

With few fresh domestic factors on the horizon, traders are looking to a slew of U.S. data next week including payrolls data and third quater gross domestic product to help set the market's near term direction.
